questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good university with a biotech programme.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, an e-mail was sent with all information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were many problems with my course registration and I send a lot of e-mails and even met up with the responsible person. However, he was not able to help very well and I had to figure out the course registration on my own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The course registration system is very bad and contains courses that are no longer available and sometimes professors change the courses without it being updated in the system. This was very frustrating and meant a lot of work for the students to find courses.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult, but at the end I found a room in a WG through the website "WG-gesucht".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a very nice living option. However, many only set their room for rent very late as they know that there is high demand and they will not have a problem finding someone to sublet it to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a housing crisis due to shortage of rooms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
- 80€ semester fee
- signing up for health care (free if you are from EU)
- Filling out a lot of documents

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always e-mail them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very unsuccessful. I had to change all my courses several times as they were not available or were overlapping with other courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open about choosing new courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very good and especially the seminars that were offered were a good opportunity to practice presentation skills.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same, but with less group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Chemical Biology
Pathogenic Microorganisms
Parasite Immunology
Polymers of Wood Science and Technology
Evolutionary Genetics of Plants and Microorganisms
Speciation From Population Genetics to Phylogenetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Chemical Biology (Interesting course on probes used in recent scientific papers for protein tagging and so on)
Pathogenic Microorganisms (about bacteria, vira and parasites)
Parasite Immunology (Very intersting about pathogens and approaches on how to cure them)
Polymers of Wood Science and Technology (less relevant for biotech, but very nice as you can choose a project to work on which can be in your field of interest and this project also counts for the grade so there is no exam)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation is really cheap with the "Deutschland ticket"

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were a lot of different sports to choose from, but also not that many spots so you had to be fast.
There were a lot of events and parties planned by ESN and ISOW which were nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visiting cities in the surroundings, going to Prague, going hiking and going to cultural events as there are many concerts available and visiting the bars and clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The same as above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's quite easy through group work. Otherwise the local and international students are very seperated during events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a custom not to do anything on Sundays except going hiking which takes some getting used to. Also, all trains are constantly delayed.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone was very friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to join Party Animals.
Be open about changing your courses.
Have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Choosing courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
